crop.notes: The clipping is columns 2-3 of page 5 only. Column 1, with the headline 'Mangled McCoole. How the Big Bruise Began and Ended Yesterday ... Allen Gets Off With One Scratch, and That On His Knuckle' and the opening sections (The Excursion, All Aboard, Who Were There, A Morning Call), is missing. The story continues on page 8 (see 470).

ocr.notes: Readable and mostly right; scattered errors ('MeCoole', 'Radn't', 'brainto', 'Tusigniticanut').

title.suggested: Allen and McCoole Enter the Ring on Chouteau Island

summary.suggested: The Missouri Republican described the excursion to the Allen-McCoole fight of September 23, 1873, on the steamer Continental to Chouteau Island, the fighters' entrance, the wrangle over a referee, and Jack Looney's selection.

metadata.notes: Page 5 header reads 'September 24, 1873'; the text calls the paper the REPUBLICAN.

facts.fact: Allen fought Mike McCoole on September 23, 1873, on the farm of Theodore Newins near Chouteau Island, the same ground as the McCoole-Davis and Allen-Davis fights; McCoole bet $1,000 against Allen's $800 at the ringside
places: Chouteau Island, Mississippi River, near St. Louis

facts.fact: Allen's seconds against McCoole were Arthur Chambers, the lightweight champion of the world, and Patsey Sheppard; Jack Looney was referee
Before the McCoole fight Allen said he would enter the ring at about 174 pounds and joked about being seconded by Barney Aaron
facts.quote: I'm the easiest man in the world to pick up, Barney Aaron seconded me once.

notes: The result is not in this clipping; the headline in column 1 says Allen won with one scratch on his knuckle, and the continuation (470) describes McCoole's defeat. The '174' weight figure is clear in the image.
